overall_prep_notes: Total prep time across all 10 manipulatives is approximately 2.5 hours. The bulk is the M1 Coin Set (printing + laminating + cutting 25 cards per pair) and the M4 Ten-Frame Mats (one per child, laminated). Plan to print and laminate over a weekend before the unit starts. Real Canadian coins can replace M1 printed cards if available — they are more durable and the handling experience is more authentic. The three character puppets (Penny, Nick, Quincy) should be printed on cardstock for years of reuse; store flat in a folder so they don't crease. Snap-cubes (M3) are a standard math-kit item; confirm you have ~600 cubes in 2-3 colours before Lesson 2.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 set of 2 pages per pair (10 pairs for a class of 20 = 20 pages).
Laminate every page before cutting. Coins get heavy K-handling across two lessons.
Cut along cut-lines. Each set has 25 coin cards (10 pennies, 6 nickels, 5 dimes, 4 quarters).
Store each set in a labelled zip-top bag with the coin counts written on the bag.
Optional: replace printed cards with REAL Canadian coins for Lesson 5. Real coins are more durable and the handling experience is more authentic.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 set per pair = 10 sets for a class of 20.

assets.name: Estimation Penny Jar
assets.purpose: Clear jar with 12-18 pennies inside, used in Lesson 1 for the estimate-then-count routine and revisited in Lesson 5 for Quincy's coin mystery.
assets.page_layout: Single letter page, portrait. A printable jar template with a clear-glass illustration; the teacher tapes pennies behind the printed jar to make a visible quantity for whole-class display.

image_placeholders.description: A large clear-glass jar illustration in B&W line-art, ~7in tall, centred on the page. The jar has a screw-top lid and clear walls. Inside the jar shape, faint dotted-line outlines suggest where pennies will sit. The teacher prints this and either tapes real pennies or draws penny circles inside.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image M2_JAR_TEMPLATE: keywords (jar, pennies, estimate) name what the template shows.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 jar template per classroom (1 page).
Laminate the page so it can be re-used across days and classes.
Use a real clear plastic jar with 12 pennies on Day 1. On Day 5 swap to 18 pennies for the Quincy challenge.
Place the jar at the carpet during Minds On for both lessons. Remove during partner work to prevent counting fatigue.
Optional: add a sticky note with each child's estimate beside the jar. Tally accuracy for diagnostic notes.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 jar template + 1 real jar with pennies for the whole class.

assets.name: Linking Snap-Cubes
assets.purpose: 30 snap-together cubes per child in 2-3 colours. Used for partner-of-5 number bonds (Lesson 2), story-problem modelling to 10 (Lesson 3), and showing coin values as cube-stacks (Lesson 5).
assets.page_layout: Not printable — these are physical cubes from a classroom kit. The page shows a labelling card for the storage bag.

image_placeholders.description: A printable storage-bag label, ~3in × 4in, in B&W line-art. Shows a small illustration of a stack of snap-cubes (red and yellow alternating) with the label 'COIN COUNTERS — Snap-cubes (30 per child, 2-3 colours)'. Includes a small Penny puppet icon in the corner.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image M3_CUBE_STORAGE_LABEL: keywords (cubes, snap-cube, label) name what the label shows.

teacher_prep_steps: Confirm you have ~30 linking snap-cubes per child in your math kit.
Sort cubes into 2-3 colours (red and yellow are ideal for partner-of-5 work).
Print and cut storage labels; tape one to each child's cube bag.
Have cubes ready in bags at the start of Lessons 2, 3, and 5.
Optional. Store red cubes and yellow cubes in separate bags for Lesson 2 to avoid mixing during distribution.
assets.quantity_per_class: ~30 cubes per child = 600 cubes for a class of 20.

assets.name: Ten-Frame Mats
assets.purpose: Laminated 2×5 grids printed at letter size. Children fill cells with cubes or pennies to model 'how many altogether' and 'how many are left' across Lessons 2, 3, and 5.
assets.page_layout: Single letter page, landscape. One large 2×5 ten-frame grid centred on the page; cells are ~2.5in square. A thin border surrounds the whole frame. A small Penny icon decorates the top-right corner.

image_placeholders.description: A large 2×5 ten-frame grid in B&W line-art on a landscape letter page. Each cell ~2.5in square, with thick black grid lines. Centered on the page. A small Penny puppet icon (~0.8in) sits in the top-right corner. Faint label 'TEN-FRAME' below the grid.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image M4_TEN_FRAME_MAT: keywords (ten-frame, cubes, pennies) name what the mat shows.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 ten-frame mat per child (20 pages for a class of 20).
Laminate every page. Children will use dry-erase markers on these mats during Lesson 5.
Stack mats at the math centre. Distribute at the start of Lessons 2, 3, and 5.
Pair each mat with a small bag of 10 round counters (or borrow cubes from M3 bag).
Optional. Print 2 mats per child if you want a 'before/after' modelling routine in Lesson 3.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 mat per child = 20 mats for a class of 20.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 page per pair (10 pages for a class of 20).
Laminate every page before cutting. Cards live in the Snack Shop play zone for the whole week.
Cut along cut-lines into 3 individual price cards per pair.
Tape one card to each Snack Shop station before Lesson 5 starts.
Optional. Replace printed cards with photos of real classroom snack items if your school runs a snack-store programme.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 set of 3 cards per pair = 30 cards total for a class of 20.

teacher_prep_steps: Print 1 page per group of 4 students (5 pages for a class of 20).
Laminate the pages before cutting. Plates need to survive the dealing rhythm in Lesson 4.
Cut along the cut-lines into 4 individual plates per page.
Keep all plates flat in a labelled folder. Distribute at the start of Lesson 4 small-group time.
Optional. Substitute real paper plates from the supply closet if your school has them in stock.
assets.quantity_per_class: 1 set of 4 plates per group of 4 = 5 sets for a class of 20.
